character_sheet: A small, vicious squid: one body block and eight tentacles fanned around it, each tentacle its own bone at its own rest angle (ModelAttackSquid.java createBodyLayer; 9 parts on a 64x32 sheet). It is a water-creature monster - 10 HP, 8 damage, no armour (MobStats.ATTACK_SQUID, AttackSquid.java:94-101) - that walks on the ground path and floats at the surface (:87), hunts players, girlfriends and boyfriends, zombies, villagers, spiders and lizards within 10 blocks (:228-267), raises the synched attacking flag and bites within 3 blocks (:193-201, doHurtTarget) and, farther out, swims at the prey while spitting from its water cannon: one throw in five, an ink sack (1 in 3) or a water ball from a muzzle 1.2 blocks ahead (:276-297). Out of water it hunts for water and dries out (:170-191); its own kind, water balls and water dragons cannot hurt it (:136-146); a Squid Zooka shot lives 250 ticks and attacks anything (:117-119, :159-168, :266). It spawns above y 50 by day (:372-376). Read it as a squid on legs: the body swaying, eight tentacles each waving at its own rate - lazily at rest, wildly on the move.

behaviour: Ten cosines, all of them always running, in two branches on the walking speed (ModelAttackSquid.java:100-122): above 0.1 every amplitude is scaled by the walking speed - pi x 0.4 (72 degrees) on the tentacles, pi x 0.04 (7 degrees) on the body; at or below 0.1 the amplitudes are fixed - pi x 0.1 (18 degrees) and pi x 0.01 (2 degrees). The rates never change: the body pitches at 0.25 and rolls at 0.39 (wingspeed 1.0, :21), the eight tentacles wave at 1.2, 1.1, 1.0, 1.9, 1.8, 1.7, 1.6 and 1.5 rad/tick (periods 3.3 to 6.3 ticks).

Each tentacle is one bone at its own rest angle (:123-130): tentacles 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 pitch (about x), tentacles 2 and 7 roll (about z); the rests are -1.03, -0.26, -1.03, +0.63, +0.6, -0.48, +0.37 and +0.43 rad. Because the eight rates are all different the tentacles drift in and out of step continuously - a squirm, never a stroke.
The body turns three quarters of the look yaw (:133), so the LookAtPlayerGoal (AttackSquid.java:89) swings the whole mantle; there is no head pitch.

The classic model never reads the attacking flag: the synched DATA_ATTACKING (AttackSquid.java:52-53) is raised within 3 blocks of prey (:196-197) and cleared when none is found (:210) - a held state - but the pose is the same either way; the bite (doHurtTarget :200) and the water cannon (:276-297) have no pose of their own.

Below the threshold the walking branch's amplitude would be 7 degrees at a speed of 0.1 against the standing branch's 18 - the code steps DOWN as the squid starts to move, then climbs to 72 degrees at full stride; the seam's speed scaling will smooth this.
